example.title: Benson culvert, county road M over an ephemeral stream west of county road 28
example.source: Wikimedia Commons (NRHP-listed structure; Category:Benson culvert (Gove County, Kansas))

brief: Twin-barrel masonry arch culvert under a gravel section-line road on the open High Plains: two semicircular arches of about 6 ft span side by side, voussoirs of dressed buff limestone, walls of squared limestone blocks laid in even courses with a plain coping, and a low solid parapet only a couple of courses above the road on each side, running straight with the road. Grass and weeds fill the dry channel; the road is crowned gravel with grassy ditches and wheat stubble to the horizon. Typical 1930s county/relief-work construction (date not in the sources).

traits.railing_detail: low solid stone parapet with flat coping
